text:
Maria: Heads-up — requesting a temporary pin of runtime 3.2.1 scoped to quant-v4 models. Observed perf regression on >2k token workloads in today's canary. Targeting a short holdback (2h) to triage. tagging @Devin @Simran for SDK/compat checks.

deploy-bot: /pin runtime 3.2.1 --scope quant-v4 --duration 2h --reason "longseq perf regression"

deploy-bot: Pin created: runtime=3.2.1 scope=quant-v4 id=pin-20260320-01 start_ts=2821234567 duration_s=7200 canaries=disabled

Devin: Quick q — do we need to pin SDK too? SDK 1.10.0 changed batch semantics; older 1.9.x clients might send legacy kv-cache headers. If gateway doesn't rewrite we could see errors.

Simran: Ran a fast smoke against SDK 1.10.0 — core path looks fine. Older clients can mis-handle the `x-kv-cache` header. Recommend a gateway shim: if header=legacy -> translate to new form. I can push a tiny rule (non-disruptive).

Oliver: If performance doesn't recover within the pin window, plan B is rollback to runtime 3.1.9. Rollback playbook: 1) canary rollback us-east-2 2) watch 15m 3) widen to remaining hosted pools. I'll own the rollback exec. Command I will run if needed:
```
/deploy rollback runtime 3.1.9 --canary us-east-2 --watch 15m
```

Frank: Also propose adding an automatic routing fallback for longseq requests -> model-variant `gptx-compat` (lower perf but stable). I can add routing rule and an eval to the regressions suite. Will also add a short SLO alert for token-p95 spike.

Maria: Sounds good. Pin is live now — please DO NOT unpin until we have perf numbers and a triage summary. @deploy-bot please keep the pin TTL and notify when 30m left.

deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Will send reminder at 2821236367 (30m left).

Simran: Gateway shim rolled to canary; monitoring shows fewer header-related errors in us-east-1 canary. Triage team continuing trace.

Devin: Adding a note in release notes draft: runtime 3.2.1 temporary holdback due to longseq perf regression; recommend customers on older SDKs upgrade to 1.10.0 or rely on gateway shim.

Maria: Thanks all. If we end up rolling back, I'll open a short postmortem and a follow-up runbook entry for quant-v4 longseq testing. For now we keep the pin and watch.

Frank: I'll attach the eval diff and SLO alert links to this thread once ready.
